title: Replying to @bryantheba an indepth look at costume design as a compar...
transcript: thank you, Brian the business analyst. because costume design is a fantastic sample set to look at in regards to genderless categories at the Tony Awards. I've talked a lot about. it's hard to compare what genderless acting categories would look like to something like directing, because directing is a field that is dominated by men, but costume design on Broadway is pretty 50 50. now, I do think it's important to note that costume design is actually a field that is dominated by women, but specifically on Broadway, it's pretty evenly split, which is a whole other conversation in and of itself. but because of the split on Broadway, that means that our eligibility pool every year would be 50 50 split. so ideally, we should see that in the number of nominees and winners throughout the years. costume design is also a great pool because it's going to be the same set of voters and nominators that genderless acting categories would have. so we could potentially see a bias pop out in this data. now, Brian, you did share some numbers in your comments. I could not replicate those, so I figured we could swap notes. so here are the numbers that I calculated. and for anybody just joining us, we were talking about the Tony Awards and gender, and I have talked extensively about this topic. so if you wanna go back, they are all in a playlist. if you mention the Brit Awards in the comments, I will block you. I'm kidding, I'm kidding. but for real, by the end of this video you will understand why it is not a good example to use. hopefully now. as Brian mentioned in his comment replies, the Tony Award for Costume Design has been split between Play and Musical since 2005. so for ease of data and because it's a decent sample set, I just took all of the nominees and winners from 2005 to present day. I based my tallies on what pronouns were used in their Wikipedia page. there were quite a few instances of people being nominated in the category twice, so I counted that as 2 tallies for their gender. and there were 2 instances of joint nominations, so I counted both of them individually. and if we run the numbers, it comes out to an almost exact 50 50 split amongst the winners for the last 17 Tonys. again, we did have a joint win for the musicals, so that's why there's one more musical winner than there are play winners. and yeah, if you look at just the musicals, it is about 40 women, a little over 60 men. but if you look at just the plays, it's more women than men. and if you look at all the winners and nominees combined, it is almost 50 50. it's 44 55. yes, there are going to be years that don't look good. like the 2019 musical nominations were all men, but then you have multiple years where it's 4 women and one man. important thing is that we have to look at the larger sample sets. because that's gonna be more indicative of what we're going to see in the long run, rather than those one offs that just prove a point.
classificationReason: Reply-to-comments video about Tony Awards genderless categories using costume design as comparison - primary purpose is responding to previous discussion, not reviewing a show
